=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:
  SPA-N-001: General liability cap
  SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
  SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
  SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
  SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
  SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of the Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics, AUD 24,000,000, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law

---

## Headline points

1. **The cover note contradicts the Seller's own Disclosure Letter.**
   - The note says Bluefen is "addressed". The letter says there is no final written consent and no evidence the conditions are met.
   - The note calls the incident "not expected to be material". The letter says scope, access and whether notification is required are all unknown.
   - We should rely only on the Disclosure Letter's statements of fact.
2. **The package removes protections the buyer would expect in any SPA.** There is no fraud carve-out. All claim categories are merged into one regime. Title is capped like an ordinary warranty. Disclosure is general rather than specific. A buyer-knowledge bar sits on top.
3. **About AUD 3.95m of value leakage is not dealt with.** This is the Riverlark facility (~3.2m), the bonuses plus on-costs (0.42m+) and the Sandbar renewals (0.33m). It belongs in the price mechanics, not in post-Completion promises.
4. **The disclosure is stale.** It speaks as at 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago. We should ask for an updated position on Bluefen, Riverlark and DD-006 before we finalise the mark-up.

---

## Summary table

| Ref | Issue | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | **Counter** |
| SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | **Counter** |
| SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | **Counter** (fallback: accept 18m with audit-cycle protection) |
| SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | **Reject** |
| SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | **Reject** (insist on carve-out) |
| SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | **Reject** |
| SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | **Reject** |
| SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | **Reject** (hard CP) |
| SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | **Reject** (payoff at Completion) |
| SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | **Reject** (treat as debt-like) |
| SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | **Reject** (broaden indemnity) |
| SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | **Reject** (specific indemnity) |
| SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | **Counter** |
| SPA-N-014 | Category separation | **Reject** |
| SPA-N-015 | Title verification | **Reject** (register alone insufficient) |
| SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | **Reject** ("settled" claim) |

---

## Issue-by-issue

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** Cap of 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A cap of 30–50% of price, or 20% only if a buyer-side W&I policy sits above it.
  - The cap must apply only to general warranties. Fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, covenants and fraud should sit outside it.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** Ask for 35%, with 20% as a fallback only if every carve-out in N-004, N-005, N-011, N-012 and N-014 is agreed. *Reason:* 20% is within market only when the serious risks sit outside the cap, and here the Seller wants them inside it.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:**
  - De minimis of AUD 25,000.
  - Basket of AUD 250,000 (about 1.04% of price), operating as a deductible: only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - De minimis of AUD 10,000–15,000.
  - Basket of about 0.5% (AUD 120,000).
  - A **tipping** basket, so recovery runs from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
  - Claims arising from related facts aggregated for the de minimis.
  - No thresholds on specific indemnities, tax, fundamentals or fraud.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** *Reason:* a deductible at the top of the market range, with no aggregation of related claims, lets connected losses (e.g., three related AUD 110k items) erode recovery.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3/13)
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. The Seller also wants every limitation to apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - 24 months for general warranties, or at minimum enough time to cover one full audited financial year after Completion.
  - Separate, longer periods for:
    - **Tax:** at least the ATO amendment period plus 6 months, with 5–7 years common.
    - **Fundamentals:** 6–7 years, aligned with the *Limitation Act 1969* (NSW).
    - **Specific indemnities:** longer periods, set item by item.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** 18 months is acceptable as a fallback, but only if the "applies to all Claims" wording is deleted. *Reason:* 18 months is market for general warranties, but the default-to-everything drafting quietly cuts tax and title claims down to 18 months.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties carry the same cap and time limit as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Fundamental warranties capped at 100% of price.
  - A time limit of at least 6–7 years.
  - No de minimis or basket.
  - No disclosure against them.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* if title fails, the buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing, so a cap of AUD 4.8m with 18 months to claim is not a real protection.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature". There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - An express statement that no limitation, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provision applies to fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers, employees, agents or advisers.
  - The buyer's rights in respect of fraud expressly preserved.
  - The non-reliance clause drafted so it does not purport to exclude statutory rights that cannot be excluded.
- **Recommendation: Reject. This is non-negotiable.** *Reason:* a seller that will not carve out its own fraud is asking the buyer to underwrite dishonesty, and no credit committee or W&I insurer will accept that.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and all public records.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Only **specific, fair disclosure**: each matter disclosed with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify its nature, scope and financial effect.
  - Data room documents treated as disclosed only where the Disclosure Letter specifically refers to them.
  - Public records limited to named searches on a specified date.
  - No disclosure against fundamentals, tax warranties or specific indemnities.
  - Disclosure that does not cure matters that are only partly described. Several entries are expressly incomplete, e.g., items 5, 6 and 8.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* general disclosure of the whole data room turns the warranties into a re-reading of the due diligence, which defeats their purpose.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the buyer or its advisers knew, or that was "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Ideally, a pro-sandbagging clause stating that the buyer's knowledge, actual or constructive, does not affect its claims.
  - At minimum, silence on the point.
  - As a last fallback only: actual knowledge of named individuals on the deal team, excluding advisers and excluding anything "discoverable".
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* combined with general disclosure, "discoverable" knowledge would knock out almost every warranty claim.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)
- **Seller:**
  - Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent.
  - Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.
  - Disclosure Letter item 2 confirms there is **no final consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met**.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A **hard Condition Precedent**: unconditional written consent from Bluefen under DD-002 cl 11.2, with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied, in a form satisfactory to the buyer (acting reasonably).
  - The Condition waivable only by the buyer.
  - Seller obligation of all reasonable endeavours or best endeavours.
  - Buyer participation in communications with Bluefen.
  - A sunset date that gives the buyer a walk right.
  - A warranty that no notice of termination or non-renewal has been received.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (~AUD 3.6m), and a consent with unmet conditions is not a consent.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)
- **Seller:** A release of the ~AUD 3.2m facility "following Completion". Disclosure item 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and the security undischarged.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A payoff letter from Riverlark Bank before Completion, plus executed deeds of release and PPSR financing-change statements (or an undertaking to lodge them) delivered **at Completion**.
  - Repayment made out of the purchase price through the funds flow, as Debt.
  - A check of whether the security extends to the shares. If it does, the release is also a title deliverable (see N-015).
  - The change-control default under cl 8.1 neutralised.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* on a debt-free basis the buyer should not pay AUD 24m for a company still subject to a AUD 3.2m secured facility and rely on a promise of a later release.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (funds flow / DD-005)
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 of Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. Disclosure item 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The bonuses plus all employer on-costs treated as **Debt or Transaction Costs**, deducted from the price.
  - Payment made through Company payroll at Completion, with PAYG withholding.
  - A specific, uncapped indemnity for any shortfall, including payroll tax, super guarantee charge and penalties.
  - The same treatment for any other change-of-control payments.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* the Company is the employer and will bear the liability after Completion, so leaving it out of the funds flow is a price reduction in the Seller's favour.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1 / DD-004, DD-010)
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment. Disclosure item 4 states:
  - Title to the Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee.
  - AUD 180,000 is recorded as open.
  - There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Preferred:** before Completion, payment of all SOW3 fees, written confirmation from Ironquay that all fees are paid, and a confirmatory IP assignment, made a Condition or a Completion deliverable.
  - **Fallback:** a specific indemnity covering *all* Loss from any failure of the Company to own or have unrestricted use of the SOW3 Project Materials. This would include infringement claims, re-development and remediation cost, and lost revenue. It would sit outside the cap, basket and disclosure, with a long time limit, supported by a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* the risk is that the Company does not own its product IP, and a payment-only indemnity covers AUD 180k of a problem that could be worth far more.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6 / DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material". Disclosure item 6 says access, scope and whether notification is required are **unknown**. Up to ~1,240 personal records were sent to an unintended external address.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Pre-Completion covenants:**
    - Complete the assessment under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act 1988 Pt IIIC).
    - Make any required OAIC and individual notifications.
    - Attempt to secure deletion or recall of the link.
    - Keep the buyer informed, with buyer review of communications.
  - **A specific indemnity** for all Loss from the incident: regulatory, remediation, claims and customer credits. It would sit outside the general cap and basket (or have a separate dedicated cap) and run for at least 3–4 years.
  - Disclosure that does not qualify the indemnity.
  - A retention or escrow until the regulatory position closes.
  - Updated incident information before signing.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* the Seller cannot both admit the facts are unknown and call the matter immaterial, so the risk should stay with the party that controlled the incident.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs". Disclosure item 8 says they should be read together and is silent on whether each is unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The contracts, plus an explanation of why one arrangement was split into three.
  - Confirmation of whether any were entered after the locked-box or accounts date, or would have needed buyer consent under the conduct-of-business covenants.
  - If they are not ordinary course or not for the Company's benefit: either a price adjustment (treated as debt-like or leakage) or Seller procurement of termination.
  - A related-party / no-leakage warranty.
  - Related items aggregated for thresholds.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** *Reason:* three identical related renewals look like splitting, possibly to stay below approval or claim thresholds, and the Seller's own letter declines to call them ordinary course.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation (cl 12.3/13 drafting)
- **Seller:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** Separately defined claim categories, each with its own limitation regime:
  - General Warranty
  - Fundamental Warranty
  - Tax Warranty / Tax Indemnity
  - Specific Indemnity (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Sandbar)
  - Covenant / Leakage
  - Fraud
- The default rule should be **reversed**: limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims unless expressly extended.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* this single sentence is the mechanism that pulls title, tax, indemnities and fraud under the general cap, basket and 18-month limit.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register. Disclosure item 10 concedes this does not confirm that the buyer has verified title.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Our own diligence:**
    - ASIC current and historical extracts.
    - Constitution and any shareholders' agreement.
    - Full allotment and transfer history.
    - No options, convertibles or ESOP entitlements.
    - A PPSR search against the Seller and the Company, including any Riverlark security over the shares.
  - **Contract:** fundamental title warranty (N-004).
  - **Completion deliverables:** executed transfers, share certificates (or indemnity for lost certificates), releases of any security over the shares, and register update.
- **Recommendation: Reject reliance on the register alone.** *Reason:* a register is the Seller's own record and does not show encumbrances or unissued rights.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** a full tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and super on the bonuses, with its own time limit (N-003) and no disclosure against it. Tax warranties sit outside the general cap.
  - **IP:** warranties on:
    - ownership of, or valid licences for, all business IP, including Ironquay SOW3;
    - employee and contractor assignment and moral rights consents;
    - open-source compliance;
    - no infringement;
    - data protection compliance, tied to DD-006.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* nothing has been agreed on tax or IP, and the "general regime" the Seller refers to is the one we are rejecting above.

---

## Other items to close (not in the list above)

- **Office lease (DD-007):** Diarise the landlord notification as a post-Completion deliverable and confirm no consent is required.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Obtain a legal view that the assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale. Also check for any change-of-control definition elsewhere in the contract.
- **W&I insurance:** If one is being considered, the positions on the cap, disclosure and knowledge (N-001, N-006, N-007) will need to match the policy terms. Insurers will exclude DD-006, Ironquay and Bluefen as known issues, so specific indemnities are needed regardless.

*This review is a working analysis for the deal team. Market ranges are indicative. Final positions should be confirmed by NSW-qualified transaction counsel against the full SPA text.*

  - An express statement that no limitation, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance provision applies to fraud, dishonesty or wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers, employees, agents or advisers.
  - The buyer's rights in respect of fraud expressly preserved.
  - The non-reliance clause drafted so it does not purport to exclude statutory rights that cannot be excluded.
- **Recommendation: Reject. This is non-negotiable.** *Reason:* a seller that will not carve out its own fraud is asking the buyer to underwrite dishonesty, and no credit committee or W&I insurer will accept that.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, the statutory registers and all public records.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Only **specific, fair disclosure**: each matter disclosed with enough detail for a reasonable buyer to identify its nature, scope and financial effect.
  - Data room documents treated as disclosed only where the Disclosure Letter specifically refers to them.
  - Public records limited to named searches on a specified date.
  - No disclosure against fundamentals, tax warranties or specific indemnities.
  - Disclosure that does not cure matters that are only partly described. Several entries are expressly incomplete, e.g., items 5, 6 and 8.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* general disclosure of the whole data room turns the warranties into a re-reading of the due diligence, which defeats their purpose.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the buyer or its advisers knew, or that was "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Ideally, a pro-sandbagging clause stating that the buyer's knowledge, actual or constructive, does not affect its claims.
  - At minimum, silence on the point.
  - As a last fallback only: actual knowledge of named individuals on the deal team, excluding advisers and excluding anything "discoverable".
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* combined with general disclosure, "discoverable" knowledge would knock out almost every warranty claim.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3)
- **Seller:**
  - Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent.
  - Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent.
  - Disclosure Letter item 2 confirms there is **no final consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met**.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A **hard Condition Precedent**: unconditional written consent from Bluefen under DD-002 cl 11.2, with all cl 11.3 conditions satisfied, in a form satisfactory to the buyer (acting reasonably).
  - The Condition waivable only by the buyer.
  - Seller obligation of all reasonable endeavours or best endeavours.
  - Buyer participation in communications with Bluefen.
  - A sunset date that gives the buyer a walk right.
  - A warranty that no notice of termination or non-renewal has been received.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (~AUD 3.6m), and a consent with unmet conditions is not a consent.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)
- **Seller:** A release of the ~AUD 3.2m facility "following Completion". Disclosure item 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and the security undischarged.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A payoff letter from Riverlark Bank before Completion, plus executed deeds of release and PPSR financing-change statements (or an undertaking to lodge them) delivered **at Completion**.
  - Repayment made out of the purchase price through the funds flow, as Debt.
  - A check of whether the security extends to the shares. If it does, the release is also a title deliverable (see N-015).
  - The change-control default under cl 8.1 neutralised.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* on a debt-free basis the buyer should not pay AUD 24m for a company still subject to a AUD 3.2m secured facility and rely on a promise of a later release.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (funds flow / DD-005)
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 of Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. Disclosure item 5 is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The bonuses plus all employer on-costs treated as **Debt or Transaction Costs**, deducted from the price.
  - Payment made through Company payroll at Completion, with PAYG withholding.
  - A specific, uncapped indemnity for any shortfall, including payroll tax, super guarantee charge and penalties.
  - The same treatment for any other change-of-control payments.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* the Company is the employer and will bear the liability after Completion, so leaving it out of the funds flow is a price reduction in the Seller's favour.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1 / DD-004, DD-010)
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment. Disclosure item 4 states:
  - Title to the Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee.
  - AUD 180,000 is recorded as open.
  - There is no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Preferred:** before Completion, payment of all SOW3 fees, written confirmation from Ironquay that all fees are paid, and a confirmatory IP assignment, made a Condition or a Completion deliverable.
  - **Fallback:** a specific indemnity covering *all* Loss from any failure of the Company to own or have unrestricted use of the SOW3 Project Materials. This would include infringement claims, re-development and remediation cost, and lost revenue. It would sit outside the cap, basket and disclosure, with a long time limit, supported by a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* the risk is that the Company does not own its product IP, and a payment-only indemnity covers AUD 180k of a problem that could be worth far more.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6 / DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter… not expected to be material". Disclosure item 6 says access, scope and whether notification is required are **unknown**. Up to ~1,240 personal records were sent to an unintended external address.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Pre-Completion covenants:**
    - Complete the assessment under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act 1988 Pt IIIC).
    - Make any required OAIC and individual notifications.
    - Attempt to secure deletion or recall of the link.
    - Keep the buyer informed, with buyer review of communications.
  - **A specific indemnity** for all Loss from the incident: regulatory, remediation, claims and customer credits. It would sit outside the general cap and basket (or have a separate dedicated cap) and run for at least 3–4 years.
  - Disclosure that does not qualify the indemnity.
  - A retention or escrow until the regulatory position closes.
  - Updated incident information before signing.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* the Seller cannot both admit the facts are unknown and call the matter immaterial, so the risk should stay with the party that controlled the incident.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008/DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are "ordinary-course operating costs". Disclosure item 8 says they should be read together and is silent on whether each is unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The contracts, plus an explanation of why one arrangement was split into three.
  - Confirmation of whether any were entered after the locked-box or accounts date, or would have needed buyer consent under the conduct-of-business covenants.
  - If they are not ordinary course or not for the Company's benefit: either a price adjustment (treated as debt-like or leakage) or Seller procurement of termination.
  - A related-party / no-leakage warranty.
  - Related items aggregated for thresholds.
- **Recommendation: Counter.** *Reason:* three identical related renewals look like splitting, possibly to stay below approval or claim thresholds, and the Seller's own letter declines to call them ordinary course.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation (cl 12.3/13 drafting)
- **Seller:** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Buyer wants:** Separately defined claim categories, each with its own limitation regime:
  - General Warranty
  - Fundamental Warranty
  - Tax Warranty / Tax Indemnity
  - Specific Indemnity (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Sandbar)
  - Covenant / Leakage
  - Fraud
- The default rule should be **reversed**: limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims unless expressly extended.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* this single sentence is the mechanism that pulls title, tax, indemnities and fraud under the general cap, basket and 18-month limit.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register. Disclosure item 10 concedes this does not confirm that the buyer has verified title.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Our own diligence:**
    - ASIC current and historical extracts.
    - Constitution and any shareholders' agreement.
    - Full allotment and transfer history.
    - No options, convertibles or ESOP entitlements.
    - A PPSR search against the Seller and the Company, including any Riverlark security over the shares.
  - **Contract:** fundamental title warranty (N-004).
  - **Completion deliverables:** executed transfers, share certificates (or indemnity for lost certificates), releases of any security over the shares, and register update.
- **Recommendation: Reject reliance on the register alone.** *Reason:* a register is the Seller's own record and does not show encumbrances or unissued rights.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - **Tax:** a full tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax, including payroll tax and super on the bonuses, with its own time limit (N-003) and no disclosure against it. Tax warranties sit outside the general cap.
  - **IP:** warranties on:
    - ownership of, or valid licences for, all business IP, including Ironquay SOW3;
    - employee and contractor assignment and moral rights consents;
    - open-source compliance;
    - no infringement;
    - data protection compliance, tied to DD-006.
- **Recommendation: Reject.** *Reason:* nothing has been agreed on tax or IP, and the "general regime" the Seller refers to is the one we are rejecting above.

## Other items to close (not in the list above)

- **Office lease (DD-007):** Diarise the landlord notification as a post-Completion deliverable and confirm no consent is required.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** Obtain a legal view that the assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale. Also check for any change-of-control definition elsewhere in the contract.
